design:
Architectural refactor of `htgr_sim_v1` separating physics, GUI and parallel
execution, so that native multithreading and **real browser parallelism** are
both supported with the physics staying in Rust.

**Full design: `docs/architecture/htgr-sim-execution.md`** (in-repo, written
with this epic). That document is the reference for implementation agents.

## The principle

> Physics kernels are deterministic, bounded, and single-threaded. Platform
> execution layers decide how independent kernels are scheduled. Native Rust
> owns native parallelism; browser JavaScript owns Web Worker parallelism;
> egui remains Rust and consumes coherent asynchronous snapshots.

## Audit findings (2026-09-06) — three of four pillars are already partly built

**Per-component kernels already exist.** `physics/` exposes `step` per
subsystem: kinetics (`kinetics.rs:328`), primary loop (`primary_loop.rs:727`,
`step_hot_leg:754`), secondary loop (`secondary_loop.rs:971`),
turbine/generator (`turbine_generator.rs:380`), whole plant
(`physics/mod.rs:757`, `step_with_correctors:775`). **The decomposition is
present; the work is making these callable without a surrounding thread.**

**The GUI boundary already exists.** `app/panels.rs:35` and `app/mod.rs:262`
document `HtgrSnapshot` as *"the only channel to the physics thread"* and
`PlantCommands` as *"the only channel into the plant model"* — already the
snapshot/controls split the target needs.

**The blocker is one function.** `src/app_scaffold/mod.rs:149`:

```rust
pub fn spawn_physics_thread<T, F>(state: SharedState<T>, mut step: F) -> JoinHandle<()> {
    thread::spawn(move || loop { step(&state); })
}
```

`thread::spawn` compiles for wasm and **panics at run time** (documented in
`scripts/check-wasm.sh`), and the `loop` lives inside the thread — so the
physics owns its own cadence and **cannot be scheduled by anyone else**: not
Rayon, not a Web Worker, not a test harness. Replacing this with a
bounded-work `tick()` driven by the platform layer is the core of the epic.

## The central risk, stated up front

The timestep DAG looks close to a **serial chain**
(controls -> kinetics -> primary -> SG -> secondary -> turbine). **A strictly
serial DAG parallelises across nothing**, and a worker pool would buy
responsiveness but not throughput.

The steam generator is documented at **~96% of compute time**, so that is where
parallelism must come from. Two implications:

- The DAG must be **measured, not assumed**. `step_with_correctors` running
  outer iterations suggests the coupling is not pure feed-forward.
- The kernel boundary must be drawn so the SG **can later be subdivided**
  (axial nodes, tube groups, enthalpy marches) without subdividing it
  prematurely.

**If profiling shows a true chain and an indivisible SG, say so and stop.** A
worker pool over a serial DAG is machinery without a purpose, and that is a
legitimate outcome to report rather than to build around.

## Relationship to existing work — this is an extension, not a parallel roadmap

| epic | relationship |
|---|---|
| **`op-eeqw` / GH #39** wasm browser demo | Phases 0-2 (toolchain, feature-gating, `web-time`) are **prerequisites**. Phase 4 (promote out of `examples/`) is shared. **Phase 3's serial fallback becomes a debug path, not the end state** — the brief is explicit that browser execution must not be permanently serial. Phases 5-9 overlap with the Pages work here and **must be reconciled, not duplicated**. |
| **`op-jyyp`** HTR-10 pebble-bed retarget | **Same files, orthogonal axis** — that epic rewrites physics content, this changes how physics is invoked. |

### Sequencing question for the maintainer

`op-jyyp` states the primary-loop model is *"a REWRITE, not a retune"*.
Extracting kernels from code about to be rewritten risks doing the work twice.

- **Architecture first** — establish the kernel contract, write the pebble-bed
  physics into a shape that already satisfies it. Costs a rebase; buys a
  correct boundary for all the new physics.
- **Physics first** — let `op-jyyp` land, then extract. Avoids churn; extracts
  from a larger body of code.

**Not decided here. Should be settled before kernel extraction starts.**

## Non-goals

Reproducing native Rayon inside one Wasm instance as the primary browser
architecture; requiring `SharedArrayBuffer` (Pages cannot serve COOP/COEP);
rewriting the egui GUI in JS/React; changing physical models or correlations;
performing the `simulators/` repository move; implementing Pages deployment
before the execution split lands.

## Branch

`develop` only. **Do not merge or push to `main`.**

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
GitHub: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/148

SEQUENCING DECIDED 2026-09-06 (maintainer): ARCHITECTURE FIRST. Establish the
kernel contract against the current prismatic physics, then write HTR-10
pebble-bed closures into that shape. Kernel extraction (op-37ke) now gates the
five op-jyyp children that rewrite htgr_sim_v1 physics modules: op-jyyp.2, .6,
.7, .8, .9. The other 13 op-jyyp children are library work (tampines, TUAS,
boon-lay, material DBs) and are deliberately NOT gated.

CONSEQUENCE: op-37ke is time-critical, not leisurely groundwork -- op-jyyp.9
(helical-coil SG) is substantial physics sitting behind it. Scope extraction to
be close to mechanical; if it is not, revisit the decision rather than letting
the SG rewrite wait.

NOTE: the reference baseline (op-fbou) is of the PRISMATIC model. It proves
extraction changed nothing and is obsolete once op-jyyp rewrites the physics.
It is NOT an HTR-10 reference -- that is op-jyyp.11.

title: htgr_sim_v1: separate physics kernels, execution runtime and GUI (native + browser parallelism)

description: Found during genfoam thermoMechanics mesh-solve port (op-p6p.11). outram-foam-basic-lib SurfaceScalarField::uniform() builds boundary patches via PatchField::zero_gradient(p.size), whose values are 0. Since scalar fvm::laplacian computes the boundary-face diffusion coeff as gamma.boundary[pi].values[fi]*area/d, a uniform gamma silently yields ZERO diffusion coefficient on every boundary face -> Dirichlet contributions dropped -> solve returns all-zeros yet reports converged (normalised_residual of x=0 with b=0 is 0). Workaround used in mesh_solve.rs: build the SurfaceScalarField with PatchField::fixed_value(size, k) boundary patches. Fix: SurfaceScalarField::uniform should set boundary values to the uniform value (fixed_value), or laplacian should treat a zero-gradient gamma patch as owner-extrapolated. Not my subtree; reporting per workspace rules.
title: basic-lib: SurfaceScalarField::uniform sets boundary face values to 0 (nulls fvm::laplacian boundary coeff)

description: CoolProp reads fluid EOS coefficients + ancillary equations from JSON (bundled/compiled). This fork hardcodes that data as Rust constants/data structures (const arrays / typed structs), so there is NO runtime file or JSON parsing and the data is rust-analyzer-navigable. Likely a codegen step (script that reads CoolProp's JSON once at authoring time and emits Rust source) rather than hand-transcription -- decide codegen vs hand-port when starting. Mirrors njoy's embedded-data-blob approach.
title: Hardcode fluid/EOS data as Rust code -- no runtime JSON/file reads

description:
In crates/kovan-literature/open/reports/nureg-cr-2671-marviken.pdf, report p.21 / PDF p.37, Table 4:2 row 7 'Initial temperature at nozzle inlet ~ degC' returns only two digits for tests 23 and 24 ('19' and '27') where every neighbouring column is three digits (T19=167, T20=181, T21=184, T22=168, T25=189, T26=135, T27=167). Both pdftotext -layout and -raw give the same truncation, so the text layer is at fault, not the extraction command. Physically the values must be three-digit.

Impact today: none. The Marviken V&V in crates/tampines-steam-tables (bead op-21g.16) does not need row 7 — it builds the stagnation state from row 6 'Min fluid temperature in the vessel' (260 degC for test 23, 230 degC for test 24), which is readable and consistent with row 5's nominal subcooling (3 K and 33 K) and with the universal stagnation qualities of Table 8:3.

Impact later: a model that wants the discharge-pipe inlet temperature rather than the vessel bulk temperature will need row 7. Fix by re-OCRing PDF p.37 at higher resolution, or by reading the page visually and recording the two values in the KovanDocument metadata. Do not guess them.
title: NUREG/CR-2671 Table 4:2 row 7 (initial nozzle-inlet temperature) is OCR-truncated for Marviken tests 23 and 24
